summary: The article explores how the Eldridgeville Community Theater (ECT) acts as an economic catalyst for local businesses in the town of Eldridgeville. Through interviews with owners and the theater's director, it shows how productions buy local supplies, boost lodging, dining and retail traffic, build business relationships and sponsorships, and foster a culture of supporting the arts. Businesses in turn support the theater through advertising and fundraising.
one_line: Eldridgeville Community Theater drives local business through supply purchases, tourism, foot traffic, partnerships and a culture of supporting the arts.
key_facts: The Eldridgeville Community Theater (ECT) is described as a hub of creativity that underpins the prosperity of Eldridgeville's local economy.
On October 3, 2023, at Miss Patty's Corner Café, the author saw patrons excitedly discussing the upcoming ECT play "Whispers of Autumn."
ECT director Nancy Thomlinson said sets use lumber from Stockwell's Timber Yard and paints from Arnold's Art Supplies, while costumes are stitched by Margaret's Dress Shop.
Jack Bernard, owner of Bernard's Bed & Breakfast, two blocks from ECT, reported more reservations during show runs, especially for last November's musical "Jazz in the Rain."
Visitors staying for shows also dined at 'The Gilded Truffle' and shopped at 'Comfy Corner Bookstore.'
Melissa Cartwright, owner of 'Mel's Vintage Boutique', hosted the launch party for ECT's seasonal schedule on September 9, 2023, which greatly increased her store's visibility and sales.
The 'Eldridgeville Echo' newspaper frequently runs features on upcoming ECT productions and the businesses that provide services to the theater.
Restaurant owner Saul Mendez noted a 30% surge in evening service receipts during show seasons.
The 'Golden Eagle Tavern' holds themed nights coinciding with ECT performances, such as a winter wonderland theme during the December run of "A Winter's Tale Retold."
Mary Schultz of 'Schultz's Fine Chocolates' said theatergoers buy her confections as after-show gifts or souvenirs.
Local businesses support ECT through playbill advertising, mutual promotion and fundraising.
The "Save the Stage" gala on December 15, 2023, drew strong local business support for the theater.
High school teacher Steven Harrow's theater arts program teaches students stagecraft and the importance of supporting local arts, leading to family outings to ECT.
